architecture.recommendation: Add object_type to the existing concepts table. Do NOT build a LEARNING_OBJECT supertype.
architecture.why: All three share every structural property already built: stable ID, canonical name, description, aliases, status, versioning, deprecation, the human-validation trigger, and the flashcard_concepts join. A supertype table would duplicate all of that and force a polymorphic foreign key in flashcard_concepts, which is strictly worse. One nullable-free column with a CHECK, defaulting to CONTENT, migrates the existing 576 rows without touching them.
architecture.guard: Content analytics MUST filter object_type = 'CONTENT'. A reasoning or quantitative object must never enter memory-versus-application content comparison. Enforced by the verifier and by a view rather than by convention.
architecture.note: concept_sections, concept_disciplines and concept_content_categories simply carry zero rows for REASONING and QUANTITATIVE objects, which is already legal. Those axes do not apply to a cross-cutting object, and an empty set is the honest representation.

list.name: Study Design Types
list.definition: Distinguishing cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, descriptive and experimental designs, and what each can and cannot establish.

list.name: Variables and Controls
list.definition: Identifying independent and dependent variables, and the role of positive and negative controls.

list.name: Randomization and Sampling
list.definition: Random assignment, random sampling, and the population/sample and parameter/statistic distinctions.

list.name: Blinding and the Placebo Effect
list.definition: Single and double blinding, why blinding matters, and the placebo response.

list.name: Bias in Research
list.definition: Systematic error introduced during data collection: selection, detection and observation bias, and how bias differs from random error.

list.name: Confounding
list.definition: A third variable influencing both exposure and outcome, and how confounding differs from bias.

list.name: Causal Inference
list.definition: Arguing from correlation to causation, and Hill's criteria including temporality and dose-response.

list.name: Validity and Reliability
list.definition: Internal versus external validity, and accuracy versus precision.

list.name: Hypothesis Formation
list.definition: Where a hypothesis comes from, how it is phrased, FINER, and the scientific method.

list.name: Statistical versus Clinical Significance
list.definition: Separating a result unlikely by chance from a change large enough to matter.

list.name: Research Settings
list.definition: Basic science versus applied and clinical settings, and the control each affords.

list.name: Significant Figures
list.definition: Counting significant digits and carrying them through arithmetic.

list.name: Exponent Rules
list.definition: Zero, negative, fractional exponents and the rules for combining powers.

list.name: Logarithm Rules
list.definition: Log identities, products, quotients, powers, and common versus natural logs.

list.name: Trigonometric Ratios and Values
list.definition: SOH CAH TOA, inverse functions, and the standard and boundary angles.

list.name: Solving Simultaneous Equations
list.definition: Substitution, elimination, and setting equations equal.

list.name: Estimation and Scientific Notation
list.definition: Calculator-free estimation, root shortcuts, and scientific notation.

list.name: Units, SI Prefixes and Scale Conversion
list.definition: Powers-of-ten prefixes and temperature scale conversion.

list.name: Direct and Inverse Proportion
list.definition: Recognising which way one quantity moves when another changes.

list.name: Measures of Central Tendency
list.definition: Mean, median and mode, and which summarises a data set best.

list.name: Measures of Spread
list.definition: Range, standard deviation, interquartile range and Bessel's correction.

list.name: Distribution Shapes
list.definition: Normal, standard normal, skewed and bimodal distributions, and the empirical rule.

list.name: Outlier Identification
list.definition: Standard-deviation and IQR rules for flagging outliers, and where outliers come from.

list.name: Probability Rules
list.definition: Independence, mutual exclusivity, exhaustiveness, and the AND, OR and at-least-one rules.

list.name: Data Display Formats
list.definition: Pie, bar, histogram, line, box plot, and log transformations of axes.

list.name: Correlation Coefficient
list.definition: Direction and strength of association, and the range of r.

list.name: Hypothesis Testing Terminology
list.definition: Null and alternative hypotheses, p-value, alpha, decision rule, Type I and II errors, confidence intervals.

CONTENT_CONCEPT.note: Bioethics is examinable Psych/Soc content, not a reasoning operation. It must be able to participate in memory-versus-application once matching questions exist.

list.name: Principles of Biomedical Ethics
list.definition: Beneficence, nonmaleficence, autonomy and justice as the four governing principles of medical and research ethics.

list.name: Informed Consent and Respect for Persons
list.definition: Honesty, consent, confidentiality, and extra protection for vulnerable participants.

list.name: Clinical Equipoise
list.definition: The genuine uncertainty between arms that makes a head-to-head trial ethical.
